---
title: 'Hosted Dev Supabase Preview'
description: 'Push migrations to a hosted dev Supabase project and share a running web and Tasks preview through Cloudflare quick tunnels.'
updatedAt: '2026-10-28'
---

Use this when a change has to be tried on a real database without a local
Docker stack, or when someone else has to click through a running build. It
covers a hosted **dev** Supabase project that the project owner has authorized
for migration pushes and test data. It never applies to production: production
migrations still go through the gated `supabase-production.yaml` workflow, and
`bun sb:push` / `bun sb:linkpush` stay off-limits in agent checkouts.

## Push migrations to the dev project

Run the repo's pinned CLI from `apps/database`. Pass the access token as
`SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`: on macOS the pinned binary can otherwise block on a
Keychain prompt with no output.

```bash
cd apps/database
export SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=<token>   # never commit it
node_modules/.bin/supabase link --project-ref <dev-ref>
node_modules/.bin/supabase db push --linked --include-all --dry-run
node_modules/.bin/supabase db push --linked --include-all
```

Read the dry run before pushing.

- **Remote-only versions.** "Remote migration versions not found" usually
  means a migration was renamed in the repo after the dev project applied it.
  Check that the renamed file is idempotent, then run
  `supabase migration repair --status reverted <old-version>` and let the
  renamed file apply.
- **Unqualified extension functions.** Without a database password, the CLI
  connects through a temporary `cli_login_postgres` role and switches to
  `postgres`. That session's `search_path` does not include `extensions`, so
  a migration that calls an extension function such as `gen_random_bytes`
  outside a function body fails with `function ... does not exist`. Apply that
  one file through the Management API (`POST /v1/projects/<ref>/database/query`,
  which runs as `postgres` with `extensions` on the path) inside a transaction.
  In the same transaction, insert its row into
  `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. Then resume `db push`.
- **API schemas.** PostgREST must expose the same schemas as
  `apps/database/supabase/config.toml` (`public, graphql_public, storage,
  private`). A project that only exposes `public` fails on `private` RPCs,
  for example task list counts on a board.

Run SQL suites such as `apps/database/supabase/tests/task-board-sprints.sql`
with `psql` over the temporary login role (`SET ROLE postgres` first). They
begin and roll back their own transaction, so the dev data is unchanged.

## Share a running preview

Keep the preview in its own detached worktree under `.worktrees/`, so feature
branches keep moving while it serves. Build only the workspace packages that
export from `dist` (`types`, `supabase`, `internal-api`, `devbox`, `editor`,
`masonry`) with their `tsc` build scripts. These are the dev runtime's
prerequisites, not release builds.

1. Start two quick tunnels first, because `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are read at
   boot. Do not override the Host header.

   ```bash
   cloudflared tunnel --no-autoupdate --url http://localhost:7803  # WEB_ORIGIN
   cloudflared tunnel --no-autoupdate --url http://localhost:7809  # TASKS_ORIGIN
   ```

2. Write each app's own `.env.local` (not the root one). Both need the
   Supabase URL, the publishable and secret keys, and the same
   `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`, plus:

   | App | Variables |
   | --- | --- |
   | `apps/web` | `BASE_URL`, `WEB_APP_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_APP_URL` = WEB_ORIGIN; `TASKS_APP_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_TASKS_APP_URL` = TASKS_ORIGIN; `TUTURUUU_EXTERNAL_APP_DOMAINS=tasks:TASKS_ORIGIN`; `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN=http://localhost:7803` |
   | `apps/tasks` | `TASKS_APP_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_TASKS_APP_URL` = TASKS_ORIGIN; `TTR_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_APP_URL` = WEB_ORIGIN; `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN=http://localhost:7803` |

   With a hosted Supabase URL, dev sign-in requires Turnstile. Use Cloudflare's
   public always-pass test keys (`NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA`,
   `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY=1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA`) and keep
   captcha off on the dev project.

3. Next 16 rejects cross-origin dev requests, and HMR reloads the page about
   every 40 seconds when its socket is refused. In the preview worktree only,
   add `allowedDevOrigins: ['*.trycloudflare.com']` to the
   `createTuturuuuNextConfig` call in `apps/web/next.config.ts` and
   `apps/tasks/next.config.ts`. Never commit it.

4. Start `bun run dev:app` in `apps/web` and `apps/tasks`. Do not use
   `bun dev`, which wraps them in portless.

Opening TASKS_ORIGIN redirects to web's login. After password sign-in, web
asks to continue to Tasks and returns through `/verify-token`. Keep the Mac
awake (`caffeinate -dimsu`) for an overnight preview. Quick-tunnel URLs change
whenever cloudflared restarts, and the env files and both apps must follow.

## Known limits

- Realtime (live board updates between people, collaborative descriptions in
  the task panel) needs the `meet-realtime` worker and its token secret. The
  preview does not run it, so the panel shows "Reconnecting".
- Sessions are tied to each quick-tunnel host. The app-session refresh fetch
  targets `https://localhost:<port>` and fails after about eight hours, so
  people have to sign in again.
- Quick tunnels allow roughly 200 in-flight requests. The first cold page
  load in `next dev` may see a few retries.
